x: If Sir Eddie had been there we would have discovered the error earlier and may well have altered our relay teams to sneak victory. Anyway, our place in the final was assured and we would put TVH to the test again.

Newham & Essex Beagles were also a target as Sir Eddie had a season's side bet with their President and was losing after the first match. As it turned out we entered the final event of the day level with Thames Valley but whereas they finished 1st, we couldn't get any of our top 400 men to the start…

Sir Eddie promised us all help, by getting our US based athletes back for the first two matches and with this promise we planned confidently for a good start and a relaxing year for the joint team managers.

The relays were a formality with a scratch sprint squad performing well to finish second and ahead of Shaftesbury – much to the delight of Sir Eddie who, it seems, this year has a side bet on with the Team Manager of Shaftesbury.

Withdrawal was a real possibility until our Patron and No.1 supporter, Sir Eddie, stepped in to meet the substantial outstanding balance. Sir Eddie travelled to Belgrade via Rome and once again gave the team tremendous support.
I say, we, because Sir Eddie had jetted into the UK just to support the team and in John Jeffery's absence he was co-opted as Joint Team Manager.
